o.text: From Proto-Turkic *kork-. Cognates include Turkish korkmak, Kazakh қорқу (qorquw), Uzbek qoʻrqmoq, Chuvash хӑра (hăra).
Internationalism; via Russian цивилиза́ция (civilizácija), ultimately from French civilisation.
From Persian سهل انگار (sahlengâr), from Arabic سَهْل (sahl, “easy”). By surface analysis, səhlən (“easiness”) + -kar.

From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (qurdamak), appended with the intensifying suffix -ələ. Cognate with Turkish kurcalamak, (Ottoman Turkish [script needed] (kurcalamak) and older Ottoman Turkish [script needed] (kurdalamak)). According to Nishanyan, ultimately of ideophonic or onomatopoetic origin, imitating the sound or motion associated with scratching or picking, to which Turkish forms like kırç ~ kırt are related.
Perhaps also influenced by the form qurd (“worm”), as the finger movement resembles a moving worm while poking/picking at something.
